name: Ehud
overview: Ehud was a male deliverer from the tribe of Benjamin, raised up by the LORD to deliver Israel from oppression. He is notably recognized for his role in killing Eglon, the Moabite king, as part of God's deliverance plan for His people. Scripture highlights Ehud's unique contribution as a divinely appointed judge and savior for Israel during a time of crisis.
namesAndTitles: The name Ehud means 'united' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name without indication of divine bestowal. This meaning may suggest a sense of unity or oneness, though the text does not elaborate further on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Ehud is identified explicitly as the son of Gera. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional family relationships for him apart from his role as a deliverer raised up by God.
scriptureSignificance: Ehud's significance lies in his divinely appointed role as a deliverer for Israel, demonstrating God's sovereignty in raising leaders to rescue His people. His courageous act of killing King Eglon was pivotal in ending Israel's subjugation and restoring peace. This narrative underlines God's faithfulness in providing salvation through unexpected means and individuals from the tribe of Benjamin.
